section: 10. reporting standard
text: Reporting standard A review of 445 LLM benchmark papers by 29 reviewers found that 16.0% "used uncertainty estimates or statistical tests to compare the results" (Bean et al., "Measuring what Matters", arXiv:2511.04703 , NeurIPS 2025 Datasets and Benchmarks).
label: core

section: 10. reporting standard
text: Their checklist asks for the sample size with a power justification and uncertainty for every primary score.
label: core

section: 10. reporting standard
text: Merged with Miller's recommendations, a result is reportable when it carries: the number of items, the number of clusters and what a cluster is; each score with its standard error in parentheses (clustered where items cluster), Wilson or Bayesian intervals below a few hundred items; for comparisons: the paired difference, its standard error and interval, and the correlation of item scores (Miller's Table 5); samples per item K, temperature, seeds, and how pass@k or the mean over samples was computed; the test used and how many comparisons were made, with the correction; the judge (model, prompt version, J judgments per item) and its parse-failure count; the minimum detectable effect, or the power for the effect claimed; the harness and its version, so the comparison can be paired by someone else.
label: core

section: 10. reporting standard
text: Tool (checked 4 October 2026) What it computes Inspect (UK AISI) stderr() CLT standard error, with cluster= ; bootstrap_stderr() ; ci() and ci_wilson() intervals; epochs for K samples per item reduced per item before the metric lm-evaluation-harness Closed-form standard error of the mean per task, bootstrap for some metrics ( bootstrap_iters ), pooled standard errors for groups; no clustering or paired comparison found evalstats (Ian Arawjo, statsforevals.com) Picks a method from the data: Wilson for 0/1 means, Bonett-Price for paired 0/1 differences, Wilcoxon for one comparison, Šidák or Romano-Wolf for many bayes_evals (Bowyer et al.) Beta-Bernoulli and hierarchical intervals for small, clustered or paired evals Lab reports are starting to print error bars: Miller singles out the Llama 3 report as an early one; Anthropic's model cards quote standard errors per trial and per task (see Topic: benchmarks , "Same model, many numbers"); arena leaderboards publish bootstrap intervals on ratings ( Human preference and arenas ).
